LLM auditresponse for ksh93.install:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `ksh93.install` script performs standard package maintenance tasks typical of AUR packages. During installation and upgrade, it ensures that the ksh-related binaries (`ksh`, `ksh93`, `rksh`, `rksh93`) are registered in `/etc/shells`, which is necessary for these shells to be usable as login shells. This is done by checking if the paths `/bin/${_ksh}` or `/usr/bin/${_ksh}` already exist in the file and appending them if not.

On removal, the script checks if any user (including root) has one of these shells set as their login shell. If root is found to be using one, it issues a warning and changes root's shell to `/bin/sh` to prevent potential lockout. It also removes the shell entries from `/etc/shells`. These actions are defensive and user-protective, not malicious. The operations are confined to expected system files and serve the legitimate purpose of shell management.

No network operations, code execution, or data exfiltration occurs. The script manipulates only system configuration files related to its own functionality, which is appropriate for a shell package. All actions align with standard packaging practices for shell software on Linux systems.
</details>
<evidence>
